summary: Francisco J. Varela worked in philosophy and other fields. He earned his MS at the University of Chile and a PhD from Harvard. His posts included the University of Chile, CNRS, and the Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital.

Sinologist and religious studies scholar Franciscus Verellen studied at Hamburg, Oxford, and under Kristofer Schipper at EPHE. He taught at EPHE and Columbia, and served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient from 1991 to 2021.
Frank E. Reynolds was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who served as a professor at the University of Chicago from roughly 1968 to 2019.
Frank F. Conlon is an indologist and historian who studied at the University of Minnesota (1969). He held the post of Professor Emeritus at the University of Washington around 2002.

Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi under teachers including Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, and Stewart Sutherland as his doctoral supervisor.

Frank Lee Woodward was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Sidney Sussex College and under Caroline Rhys Davids, he served as head of Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translated for the Pali Text Society in 1919.

Frank Raymond Allchin worked in Indology and archaeology. He studied at SOAS under Kenneth de Burgh Codrington, taught Indian archaeology at SOAS (1954–1959), held Indian Studies posts at Cambridge (1959–1989), and co-founded the Ancient India and Iran Trust.

Frank-Richard Hamm worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate under Walther Schubring at the University of Hamburg (1940–1948), later teaching there (1948–1964) and becoming a professor at the University of Bonn in 1965.

Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Salisbury Professor at Yale University (1926–1953).

Franz Altheim worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Goethe University Frankfurt, he held posts there (~1928–1938), at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1938–1950), and at the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1964).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Chicago and served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

Franz Bernhard was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and at Frankfurt, later serving as professor at the University of Hamburg from 1966 to 1971.

Franz Boas was a linguist and scholar who studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at Clark University, the Smithsonian Institution, the American Museum of Natural History, and Columbia University (~1896–1936).

Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Paris under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and at Göttingen. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1821 to 1867.
Franz Ferdinand Schwarz was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Graz from 1952 to 1958 and served as a professor there from around 1974 to 1999.

Franz Heinrich Trithen was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the British Museum (~1844–1848) and was professor of modern languages at the Taylor Institution (~1848–1854).

Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist who studied at Göttingen, Breslau, and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Deccan College (1866–1881) and the Chair of Indology at Göttingen from 1881.

Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bonn, Halle, and under Franz Bopp in Berlin. From 1829, he taught Oriental languages at Humboldt University of Berlin, becoming an extraordinary professor of theology in 1831.
Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist who earned master's degrees from Freie Universität Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, and a PhD from the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

Franz von Erdmann was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Rostock (1810–1814) and held a post at Kazan Imperial University from roughly 1818 to 1845.
